messages:
incidents-bot: Paging oncall - high error rate observed for /api/v1/generate on host pool 'gpu-prod-eu'
Sam T.: on it, seeing 5xx spikes, graphs?
Mia K.: Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ops/serving?panel=queue_depth - queue depth jumped to ~2.8k at 06:12 UTC
Arjun R.: HPA logs show scale events at 06:13 -> attempted to scale to 30 pods but cluster had only 22 GPUs free; k8s pending pods piling in Pending state
Sam T.: confirm. kubectl get pods -n serving | grep Pending
Sam T.: ```
NAME                                READY STATUS    RESTARTS AGE
model-variant-abc-7f8b9c          0/1  Pending   0        3m
model-variant-def-5d4a3b          0/1  Pending   0        2m
```
Jess L.: warmup logs show long coldstart KV cache priming for large models, single warmup took 45s which made queued requests wait
Mia K.: timeline: 06:11 anomaly detection alert -> 06:12 queue spike -> 06:13 HPA triggered -> 06:14 pods Pending due to GPU shortage -> 06:15 tail lat increase -> 06:17 higher error rate
Arjun R.: hypothesis 1: autoscaler attempted scale but cluster capacity exhausted (GPU pool saturation). hypothesis 2: warmup delay magnified tail latency during scale and backpressure led to queue growth
Sam T.: mitigation applied: rerouted low-priority traffic to smaller/quantized variant (model-variant-quant) at 06:18
Sam T.: also increased burst pool by 2 gpus (manual allocation) at 06:20 which allowed 6 pods to schedule
Mia K.: immediate effect: queue depth dropped from 2800 -> 400 over ~3 minutes, error rate stabilized
Jess L.: logs attached: (pasted snippets) ```ERROR serving: request dropped due to queue timeout after 30000ms
WARN warmup: priming kv entries took 45213ms
```
Arjun R.: open actions for RCA: collect kube events for 06:00-06:25, HPA controller logs, GPU pool allocation timeline, warmup latency traces per model, and the prefix cache priming trace
Sam T.: assigning owners: Arjun - kube events + HPA logs; Mia - queue and metrics graphs + timeline; Jess - warmup traces and kernel/runtime logs
Mia K.: short handoff for next oncall (12:00 UTC): Incident mitigated, customer impact: several customers saw timeouts for ~6-10min, no data exfiltration; follow-up: prioritize autoscaler improvement and pre-warming heuristics
Sam T.: adding note: consider lowering HPA cooldown or pre-warming when queue depth > 500 for heavy models
Jess L.: will open ticket with reproducer and add EV to Optimize team for caching priming optimization
incidents-bot: Pager note recorded, severity downgraded to P2 at 06:29 UTC
Sam T.: thanks team, handing off to Mia for RCA writeup and postmortem. 
Mia K.: I'll compile timeline + logs and post back in this thread by EOD
